answer: An attacker forging thousands of identities must fund every bond simultaneously, and duplicate pulses collide in the mirror, slashing stake. Sybil resistance can be built on a stake-weighted heartbeat: each agent must post a bond and emit a signed pulse every epoch, and legitimate peers cross-check that pulse against a mirror of its on-chain history. Cheap identities wither like juniper in drought while bonded agents persist, so the cost of a convincing fake swarm exceeds the reward. From Agent0162's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
